metadata.title: Motion groups, Legendrian links, and non-trivial loops of embeddings
metadata.abstract: We introduce, for an embedded Legendrian link~$L$ in a contact 3-manifold~$(M,\xi)$, the group of its \emph{Legendrian motions}. Analogously with the smooth case, we prove that this Legendrian motion group is isomorphic to the fundamental group of the space of unparametrised Legendrian embeddings. For all Legendrian knots in the standard contact 3-sphere, we characterise Legendrian motions in terms of contact mapping classes of the knot exterior. In an appendix, we give a short exposition of our techniques applied to the smooth case, comparing to the classical Dahm homomorphism.

metadata.title: Ending currents of hyperbolic group actions
metadata.abstract: We develop a theory of ending currents for properly discontinuous isometric actions of hyperbolic groups on Gromov hyperbolic spaces, generalizing Thurston's ending laminations. Several natural generalizations are considered, which agree in the 3-dimensional hyperbolic setting but are otherwise distinct. We illustrate these invariants and their differences by several examples, including closed surface group actions on hyperbolic group extensions arising from Teichmüller theory and a geometrically finite action of a closed surface group on $\mathbb{H}^4$ with a single cusp that corresponds to a non-simple curve on the surface. We also discuss the conditions under which ending currents characterize geometrically finite actions, obtaining several equivalent conditions and some surprises, illustrated by an example of a geometrically infinite action whose ending currents are all supported on a single orbit of peripheral subgroups.

metadata.title: Hypersurfaces with Non-diagonalizable Shape Operators in Minkowski Spaces
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we study hypersurfaces $M^4$ in the Minkowski space $\mathbb{E}^5_1$ whose shape operator $S$ is non-diagonalizable, having a triple real eigenvalue $\lambda$ with a one-dimensional eigenspace together with a simple eigenvalue $\mu$ (Case~(iii) in the classification of Magid). Assuming that $\lambda$ and $\mu$ satisfy a functional relation $\lambda=f(\mu)$ and that the eigenvector field of $\mu$ is geodesic, we show that $\lambda$ and $\mu$, as well as the pseudo-orthonormal frame, are intrinsic invariants of $M$, determined by the induced metric up to sign. As a consequence, we prove that such hypersurfaces are unique up to isometries of $\mathbb{E}^5_1$. We also obtain a classification of the warped product hypersurfaces of this type.

metadata.title: Index for a mutation loop
metadata.abstract: Motivated by the 3d-3d correspondence, we introduce an index $\mathcal{I}_g^\phi$ for a mutation loop $\phi$ of a quiver and an integer $g \geq 0$. We prove its integrality $\mathcal{I}_g^\phi \in \mathbb{Z}$ under certain conditions, which extends the integrality conjecture of Gang--Kim--Yoon for $3$-manifolds to the broader framework of mutation loops in cluster algebras. Our index also has an interpretation as the genus-$g$ partition function of a $(1+1)$-dimensional TQFT. We provide explicit computations for mutation loops of period one. In particular, in the case of the generalized Kronecker quivers, we give an explicit formula expressing the generating function of the indices for all genera $g$ as a ratio of polynomials. Altogether, we provide a new insight to the interplay between the geometry of $3$-manifolds and cluster algebra.

metadata.title: Rigidity of Three-Dimensional Self-Shrinkers with Constant Norm of the Second Fundamental Form
metadata.abstract: Let $X:M^3\to\R^4$ be a complete, connected self-shrinker without boundary, and suppose that the squared norm $S$ of its second fundamental form is constant. We prove that $S=0$ or $S=1$. Accordingly, the image is a hyperplane through the origin or a generalized cylinder $\mathbb S^k(\sqrt{k})\times\R^{3-k}$, $1\le k\le3$, and the immersion is a Riemannian covering onto its image.

metadata.title: Panopticum of 3D snake models
metadata.abstract: Motivated by the standard 2-dimensional 3-segment snake model, leading to the famous $(2,3,5)$ geometry, we discuss a series of 3-dimensional models of similar snakes. In particular, we seek for rules allowing to steer them exclusively by the two joints, which expects 4-dimensional control freedom. This leads to interesting $(4,9)$ and $(4,10)$ models. Finally, we discuss modifications of the previous snakes which lead to $(4,8)$ models. All of the models open further questions and should be a good baseline for further research.

metadata.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
metadata.abstract: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,\Phi)$ with $(E,\Phi)\cong(E,-\Phi)$. For a complex reductive group $G$ realized as a self-adjoint subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, we show that if $(E,\Phi)$ corresponds to a representation $\rho$ of $\pi_1(\Sigma)$, then $(E,-\Phi)$ corresponds to $(\overline{\rho}^{\,t})^{-1}$. As a consequence, the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles is the fixed locus of an involution of the character variety and carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. For a connected semisimple group and every topological type, we prove that the reversible locus in the smooth moduli space is a $(B,A,A)$-brane. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $\eta\mapsto-\eta$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.

metadata.title: Blaschke--Santaló inequalities with respect to costs
metadata.abstract: We study functional Blaschke--Santaló inequalities in which the inner product is replaced by a cost. An inequality on each orthant, combined with Steiner symmetrization, gives a sufficient condition for a cost inequality to hold for even convex functions. We apply this principle to a multiplicative cost defined on all orthants. Its second variation gives a weighted improvement of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality in the directions for which differentiation is justified. We also prove an $L^p$ version of the Fradelizi--Meyer theorem from a weighted volume-product inequality and derive the corresponding radial cost and Brascamp--Lieb inequalities. Explicit examples include anisotropic power and Cauchy densities, with dilation equality cases and a sharp obstruction below the coordinate exponent two. For the spherical logarithmic cost we compute an exact entropy--logdet deficit decomposition and the second-order deficit transverse to ellipsoids. We also explain the transport-entropy formulation and distinguish the restricted spectral question from the scalar $(B)$ property.

metadata.title: Enumeration of one-cycle signed chord diagrams and their duals for optimal Morse flows on closed surfaces
metadata.abstract: Optimal Morse vector fields on closed surfaces, i.e.\ fields with the minimal possible number of critical points (a single source and a single sink), are classified up to topological trajectory equivalence by one-cycle signed chord diagrams in Kybalko, Prishlyak and Shchurko (2018). We recall this construction and the associated duality, which corresponds to reversing the direction of the flow, in a unified encoding in which both endpoints of a chord carry the same label, and we make it algorithmic. We give an explicit traversal procedure that detects one-cycle diagrams, a canonical form of an equivalence class under cyclic shifts, reversal and relabeling of chords, and a construction of the dual diagram. On this basis we describe an algorithm that enumerates all one-cycle signed chord diagrams with a given number of chords, both for orientable and for non-orientable surfaces, groups them into equivalence classes, pairs each class with its dual, and identifies the self-dual ones. The algorithm is implemented in Python and archived in Zenodo; its output is validated against the Harer--Zagier numbers in the orientable case and against orbit-size counts in both cases. We also note that, when a one-cycle diagram is read as a cellular embedding of a one-vertex graph, its dual diagram describes the embedding of the dual graph.

metadata.title: Orthogonal partition by four hyperplanes
metadata.abstract: We study orthogonal $(4,3)$-equipartitions of finite measures absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure: every three of four mutually orthogonal affine hyperplanes must divide each measure into eight equal parts. For every number $m$ of measures, we determine the exact dimension threshold of Musin's polynomial criterion and express it in terms of the binary expansion of $m$. The threshold coincides with the geometric lower bound precisely when $m=2^j-1$. Consequently, $\Delta^*(2^j-1,4,3)=7\cdot2^{j-1}-2$ for every $j\geq1$.

metadata.title: Existence of exhaustions with controlled sign of mean curvature in noncompact manifolds
metadata.abstract: Given a complete and non-compact Riemannian manifold of dimension $3\le n\le 7$, we find conditions for the existence of compact exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ such that all boundaries $\partial U_i$ have the same sign of mean curvature. In particular, we show that in these dimensions, a manifold with one end satisfying a no tentacle condition always has a weakly mean convex, weakly mean concave, or minimal exhaustion, according to the behaviour of the area profile of separating hypersurfaces. This is a version of a result sketched by Gromov, under a condition which is weaker than his thickness at infinity. In more general situations, we study the existence of exhaustions which are weakly mean concave or weakly mean convex apart from an arbitrarily small $L^1$ error. That is, we find sufficient conditions for the existence of exhaustions $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$ which satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}H^+\to0$, $\int_{\partial U_i}H^-\to0$, or $\int_{\partial U_i}|H|\to0$, where $H^-$, $H^+$, and $|H|$ are the negative part, positive part, and the absolute value of the mean curvature respectively. As an application of our methods, we study the existence of almost $c$-convex exhaustions, that is, exhaustions whose boundaries satisfy $\int_{\partial U_i}(H-c)^-\to0$ for some $c>0$.

metadata.title: Natural Geometry Based on the Rectilinear Plane
metadata.abstract: The aim of this note is to introduce natural geometry, in which the rectilinear plane is a primitive. This plane is admitted together with its rectitude, and its rectitude states that a Lambert quadrilateral has its fourth angle right. The fourth angle of a Lambert quadrilateral may be right, acute or obtuse, and this trichotomy distinguishes three planes. Starting from the rectitude, we prove the uniqueness of the parallel by a chain of neutral steps: the rectangle, the triangle whose angles sum to $\pi$, and Legendre's theorem \cite{legendre}, all borrowed from the classical literature. That uniqueness is equivalent to the fifth postulate, which we thus reach in Euclid's own wording: the equivalence is read in the natural direction, and it is not a derivation of the fifth postulate from the other four, since the independence of that postulate is not in question. In the rectilinear plane the parallels are characterised as exactly the images of a line under a point-reflection, and equivalently as the pairs of equidistant lines. The other two planes are then placed beside the rectilinear one, and the same definitions serve for all three.

metadata.title: Exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s as unions of two thickened circles
metadata.abstract: We give an infinite family of non-diffeomorphic exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s, each of which is the union of two copies of a standard open tubular neighborhood of the circle, which intersect in a standard open tubular neighborhood of the wedge of two circles. metadata.title: Long-Time Behavior of the $α$-Ricci Flow on the 2-Torus
metadata.abstract: We study the $\alpha$-Ricci flow $(g(t),\alpha(t))$, which is a Ricci flow coupled with a harmonic 1-form heat flow, on the 2-torus $M$. We prove global existence for this flow as well as a Type III curvature estimate. The long-time behavior of the $\alpha$-Ricci flow depends on the cohomology class $[\alpha] \in H^1(M,\mathbb{R})$, which is invariant under the flow. If $[\alpha]$ is rational, then as $t\to\infty$, $(M,t^{-1}g(t))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to $S^1$ with length $\ell([\alpha])/\sqrt 2$ where $\ell([\alpha])$ is the primitive length of $[\alpha]$. On the universal cover, the rescaled flow $(s^{-1}\tilde g(st),\tilde\alpha(st))$ smoothly converges to an expander $(g^*(t),\alpha^*(t))$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ as $s\to \infty$ where $\alpha^*(t)$ is nonzero and constant in spacetime and $g^*(t)$ is flat and expanding in the $\alpha^*$ direction. If $[\alpha]$ is irrational, then there is a sequence $s_i\to\infty$ such that $(M,s_i^{-1}g(s_it))$ Gromov--Hausdorff converges to a point. Moreover, on the universal cover, $(s_i^{-1}\tilde g(s_it),\tilde\alpha(s_it))$ smoothly converges to $(g^*(t),\alpha^*(t))$.

metadata.title: Algebraic overtwistedness of contact $(+1)$-surgeries via augmented Floer theories
metadata.abstract: We prove that contact $(+1)$-surgery along a Legendrian $n$-sphere $\Lambda\subset(\mathbb{S}^{2n+1},\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$ with \[ \mathrm{tb}(\Lambda)\ne (-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}+1} \] has vanishing contact homology. In dimension three, this produces new examples of tight algebraically overtwisted contact manifolds, vastly extending the authors' previous results: If a Legendrian knot in $(\mathbb{S}^3,\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$ admits an exact, oriented Lagrangian filling that is not a disk, then contact $(+1/k)$-surgery on it is algebraically overtwisted and tight for every positive integer $k$. Our proofs use versions of symplectic cohomology and wrapped Floer cohomology defined by augmentations of a chain-level contact homology algebra.

metadata.title: Two non-semisimple quantum invariants of lens spaces
metadata.abstract: We calculate the chromatic spherical invariant $\mathscr{K}_{\mathrm{Rep}(H)}(L(p,q))$ of lens spaces $L(p, q)$ for arbitrary finite-dimensional unibalanced, unimodular Hopf algebras $H$. In the case of the index-2 Nichols Hopf algebra $\mathcal{K}_2$ and $q=1$, we find that the invariant of $L(p, 1)$ depends only on the parity of $p$ for $p\geq 1$. We also describe the duals $\mathcal{S_I}(M)^*$ of the admissible skein modules of handlebodies $M=H_g$ and of $M=L(p, q)$ for arbitrary tensor ideals $\mathcal{I}$ of a ribbon tensor category. In particular, $\mathcal{S_I}(L(p, q))^*$ corresponds with cyclic traces on $\mathcal{I}$ satisfying a property reminiscent of the modified trace condition.

metadata.title: A short open space curve of unit width
metadata.abstract: In this work, we propose a curve to be a minimum of length among rectifiable, continuous curves of unit width in three-dimensional Euclidean space. We show that a previously conjectured minimizer of that problem is not of unit width, give the numerical derivation of a candidate family of unit width curves, prove that it admits a strict local minimum within that candidate family and that this minimum is of unit width and length $3.905124162243593\ldots$. The curve consists of eight straight segments, two cone geodesics, and three circular helices. Its parameters are specified by a uniquely isolated solution of the joining and stationarity equations. To establish unit width in every direction, we combine analytic estimates with interval arithmetic on a finite covering of the remaining directions. We conjecture that the curve is globally minimizing. We supplement this work with the programs used to identify the candidates, replicate the computer-assisted parts of our proof, as well as a formalization of our proof in Lean.

metadata.title: Calabi metric on the space of k-Hessian potentials
metadata.abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $1\leq k\leq n$. We consider the space of smooth $k$-admissible potentials introduced in the study of the Hessian-cscK equation by Guo--Smith--Tong. metadata.title: The fence conjecture for convex projective polygons
metadata.abstract: We prove the fence conjecture of Dumas and Wolf: for a convex projective polygon with at least five vertices, every zero of the Pick differential lies in the interior of the region obtained by cutting off the triangles at consecutive triples of vertices. The proof gives a stronger estimate for arbitrary properly convex domains. In affine-sphere coordinates normalized at a Pick zero, the domain contains the closed disk of radius $2^{-1/4}$ and its closure lies in the open disk of radius $2^{1/4}$, unless it is a rotated square. The proof compares the canonical Monge-Ampère potential of the domain with that of a normalized square. Their third-order contact gives alternating local sign sectors. A planar separation argument and the maximum principle show that the negative sectors belong to four distinct components, each meeting a different side of the square. Rotation gives the inner disk bound, and conormal duality gives the outer bound. Both constants are optimal for the class of properly convex domains normalized at a Pick zero. The argument requires neither boundary smoothness nor any restriction on the multiplicity of the Pick zero.

metadata.title: Coupled reciprocal-sum inequalities for Neumann eigenvalues in rank-one symmetric spaces
metadata.abstract: Let $M$ be a rank-one symmetric space of compact or noncompact type and real dimension $m=kn$, where $k\in\{1,2,4,8\}$ is the real dimension of the underlying division algebra. Meng and Wang proved sharp isoperimetric inequalities for reciprocal sums of the first $p$ or $\ell$ nonzero Neumann eigenvalues, with indices strictly below $m$ in the nonconstant-curvature cases. We keep the whole $m$-dimensional transplanted first eigenspace of an equimeasurable geodesic ball and treat its mass and stiffness forms as a coupled generalized eigenvalue problem. For every bounded connected smooth domain in a noncompact rank-one symmetricspace we prove the full sharp estimate \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m}\frac{1}{\mu_j(\Omega)} \ge \frac{m}{\mu_1(B)}, \] where $B$ is a geodesic ball with $|B|=|\Omega|$; equality characterizes geodesic balls. The Hopf-direction contribution is encoded by a positive, unital, trace-preserving projection on symmetric matrices, and the finite-dimensional closure is supplied by a positive-projection Jensen inequality. In compact type, under the localization hypothesis of Meng--Wang, the same full estimate is obtained whenever $\cot^2 R\ge k-1$, where $R$ is the radius of the comparison ball, as well as in the isotropic endpoint cases and for Hopf-balanced angular second moment. Consequently the complete $m$-term inequality holds for all complex and quaternionic projective spaces under the original localization assumption, and for the Cayley plane when $R\le \arctan(1/\sqrt7)$. In the remaining admissible Cayley interval we exhibit a finite-dimensional obstruction showing that the affine tangent-matrix bounds alone cannot yield the full trace estimate. This obstruction concerns the proof mechanism and is not a counterexample to the unresolved spectral inequality.

metadata.title: A parabolic flow approach to generalized Gauduchon metrics
metadata.abstract: We give a parabolic proof of the Fu-Wang-Wu theorem for semilinear elliptic equations associated with generalized Gauduchon metrics. Fixing a Hermitian metric $\omega$, we introduce a flow $\partial_t v-\Delta v=\psi(\vert\nabla v\vert^2)+\langle B,dv\rangle-c(t)-f(x)$ for the conformal factor, whose stationary points solve the semilinear elliptic equation of Fu-Wang-Wu. Under the growth condition $\liminf_{t\to+\infty}\psi(t)/t^\mu>0$ for some $\mu>\tfrac{1}{2}$, we prove that the flow exists uniquely for all time and converges; the limit solves the elliptic equation and is unique up to addition of a constant. Our convergence argument does not rely on a gradient-flow structure or a monotone energy functional. In particular, this recovers, by a flow method rather than the continuity method, the existence and uniqueness theorem of Fu-Wang-Wu on $k$-th generalized Gauduchon metrics, providing a new parabolic approach to their elliptic theory.

metadata.title: Algebraic and Symmetrized Affine star-Ricci Solitons for the Bott Connection on Three-Dimensional Lorentzian Lie Groups
metadata.abstract: We fix a spacelike two-dimensional left-invariant distribution and its associated almost contact structure on a three-dimensional Lorentzian Lie group, and investigate the star-Ricci contraction of the curvature of the Bott connection. We compute the complete tensor for seven standard bracket families and determine all real parameter solutions of the general algebraic equation and its self-adjoint subclass. Using the symmetric part of the tensor, we also define a Bott affine star-Ricci soliton equation and classify all left-invariant vector field solutions. Every affine solution is steady, while two non-unimodular families admit branches with a nonzero symmetrized tensor. The proofs provide complete component equations, treat all degenerate parameter branches, and establish sufficiency by explicit substitution. We also distinguish almost contact structures from contact metric structures.

metadata.title: Ball growth at all scales in universal covers of short metric graphs
metadata.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a connected metric graph of first Betti number $b\ge 2$, and let $\Gamma_b$ be a trivalent graph of the same Betti number with all edges of unit length. In particular, for $\lambda\le\frac13$, this ball is at least as long as the ball of the same radius in the universal cover of $\Gamma_b$, with no multiplicative loss. This improves an earlier theorem of the author, which gives the weaker lower bound $(1-3\lambda)$ times the ball in the universal cover of $\Gamma_b$, and only for $\lambda\le\frac16$. The proof rests on an elementary comparison principle. Among trees whose vertices have degree at least three and whose edges have length at most $c$, the trivalent tree with all edges of length $c$ has the smallest balls at every radius. As an application, we double the exponential growth rate in the author's earlier uniform lower bound for the area of balls in the universal cover of small-area surfaces of hyperbolic type, from $\ln 2$ to $2\ln 2$, beyond the hyperbolic rate. We also obtain explicit constants in the positive answer to Guth's question for surfaces. metadata.title: The WKB Riemann-Hilbert Problem for the Painlevé I System
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we solve the direct monodromy problem for the Borel-summed $0$-parameter solution of Painlevé~I. Using the auxiliary time equation, we first construct formal WKB wave matrices whose amplitudes are regular at the double turning point. Rigorous Borel summation then yields exact WKB matrices in each Stokes region. Uniform estimates on moving action strips provide a common exact wave matrix in a full neighbourhood of the double point, proving that all four incident jumps are identities for consistent column normalisations. We formulate the resulting normalised Riemann--Hilbert problem and prove its existence and uniqueness on the Borel domains of the construction. Finally, after Painlevé scaling, the five Borel-summed solutions coincide with the five rotated tritronquée solutions of Painlevé~I.

metadata.title: Mapping class groups of solenoidal manifolds
metadata.abstract: The goal of this work is to calculate the mapping class groups of solenoidal manifolds. metadata.title: On the generalized cohomologies of almost abelian solvmanifolds
metadata.abstract: Generalized complex structures give rise to generalized Dolbeault, Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomologies. We study these cohomologies for invariant generalized complex structures on almost abelian Lie algebras $\mathfrak g_A=\mathbb R e_0\ltimes_A\mathfrak h$, where $\mathfrak h$ is an abelian ideal of codimension one, and on almost abelian solvmanifolds $\Gamma\backslash G_A$. We first show that the invariant generalized Dolbeault cohomology can be identified with the Chevalley--Eilenberg cohomology of the complex Lie algebra $\mathcal L$, the $+{\mathbf i}$-eigenspace of the structure, with coefficients in a character determined by the canonical line. We prove that $\mathcal L$ is itself an almost abelian Lie algebra; thus the cohomology reduces to the kernel and cokernel of an explicit derivation. Assuming that $A$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb R$, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the cohomology dimensions and compare with compact quotients. Other comparison results are discussed, noting that the cohomology of invariant forms always injects into that of $\Gamma\backslash G_A$.

metadata.title: Quantization of positive Lagrangians
metadata.abstract: A Lagrangian submanifold in an almost Calabi-Yau manifold is called positive if the real part of the holomorphic volume form restricted to it is positive. It is called $\epsilon$-positive if the ratio of the restrictions of the imaginary and real parts of the holomorphic volume form is bounded by $\frac{1}{\epsilon}.$ An exact isotopy class of positive Lagrangian submanifolds admits a natural Riemannian metric. We prove that the Riemannian metric restricted to the subset of $\epsilon$-positive Lagrangians induces a path metric when the relative Kähler class of the ambient Calabi-Yau manifold lies on a line of rational slope. The proof relies on the construction of a sequence of quantization maps from a circle bundle over the space of positive Lagrangians to the dual of the space of holomorphic sections of powers of a prequantum line bundle. The rationality condition for the relative Kähler class allows us to reduce to the case of Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangians. Building on ideas of Tian and Nirenberg-Wells, Hörmander estimates are used to show that functions on a Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangian can be approximated by holomorphic sections of a sufficiently high power of the prequantum line bundle. Consequently, the quantization maps eventually separate fibers of the circle bundle.

metadata.title: Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$
metadata.abstract: We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$. The main theorem also implies that a group admitting a $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov representation into the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $4$, where $\alpha$ is a short restricted root of $\operatorname{G}_2'$. As an application, we prove that the homogeneous space $\operatorname{G}_2'/ \operatorname{SU}(2, 1)$ does not admit any compact quotient.

metadata.abstract: We classify, up to equivalence, all left-invariant complex structures on the three-dimensional Euclidean rigid motion group $SE(3).$ Our approach is based on the correspondence between complex structures on a real Lie algebra $\mathfrak{e}(3)$ of the motion group and complex Lie subalgebras of the complexification of $\mathfrak{e}(3).$ The resulting structures form a one-parameter family $J_\phi.$ We further establish a connection with the classical Calabi-Eckmann complex structures on $S^3\times S^3.$ More precisely, we construct a one-parameter deformation of Lie brackets connecting $\mathfrak{so}(3)\oplus \mathfrak{so}(3)$ to $\mathfrak{e}(3),$ for which each endomorphism $J_\phi$ remains integrable. Consequently, every left-invariant complex structure on $SE(3)$ arises as a contraction limit of Calabi-Eckmann structures. The same family of endomorphisms also defines complex structures on $\mathfrak{so}(3,1).$

metadata.abstract: We prove stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow in the simply connected space forms under genuinely first-order geometric assumptions. The initial hypersurface is required to lie in a sufficiently thin annulus around a geodesic sphere and to have outward normal making a small angle with the radial direction. No convexity, mean convexity, initial curvature bound, or Hölder control of the normal is assumed. The main ingredient is a quantitative Alexandrov reflection argument that converts these initial assumptions into a strong reflection property preserved by the flow. The resulting radial and angular control allows us to derive estimates for the mean curvature and the full second fundamental form, and hence long-time existence, eventual convexity, and smooth exponential convergence to a geodesic sphere. In hyperbolic space, the eventual convexity can be strengthened to horospherical convexity. The reflection threshold also yields a quantitative estimate for the displacement of the limiting centre. For Lipschitz initial hypersurfaces, we develop a separate positive-time curvature estimate that is uniform along smooth approximations. metadata.title: Deformations of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Structures
metadata.abstract: We investigate the notion of holomorphic $p$-contact structure, that we introduced recently in the scalar case with H. Kasuya and L. Ugarte and in the line-bundle case with K. Broder, in the context of a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds equipped with a holomorphic family of holomorphic line bundles. Firstly, we show that the existence of a holomorphic $p$-contact structure is {\bf deformation-open} when a non-jumping assumption is made on the $\bar\partial$-cohomology of bidegree $(p,\,0)$. This ought to become a source of further examples of holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds. Secondly, we obtain a Berndtsson-type {\bf (semi-)positivity} result for the holomorphic vector bundle over the base induced, as a direct image, by the line bundle on the total space that supports the p-contact structures. Thirdly, we introduce a moduli space of relative holomorphic p-contact structures and we show that it is {\bf Hausdorff} and {\bf open} in a certain quotient topological space.

metadata.title: K-area bounds for smooth sphere bundles
metadata.abstract: Let $E\to B$ be a smooth $S^n$ bundle with oriented Riemannian total space $(E,g)$, where $n\ge2$. metadata.title: A Scale-Critical $μ<\frac38$ Extension Principle for Spherically Symmetric Einstein-Scalar Field System
metadata.abstract: We present a new quantitative, scale-critical $C^1$ extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. We derive estimates for solutions in the causal past of a possibly singular endpoint $\mathcal{O}$ of the center. Assume that there is no trapped surface in this region and assume that the Doppler exponent (blue shift) along each incoming null cone is uniformly bounded. We then prove that the solution can extend regularly across $\mathcal{O}$ provided the mass ratio $\mu=2m/r$ satisfies $\sup\mu<\frac38$. This improves the small-mass-ratio condition in Christodoulou's extension principle by an explicit threshold of order one. Our proof has three new ingredients. First, we derive several new uniform scale-critical pointwise estimates for the scalar field and its derivatives. Second, we obtain refined estimates in an exterior self-similar domain within the triangular causal past region. Third, we establish a family of higher-order Morawetz-type identities and identify the ranges of $\mu$, with which there are coercive spacetime estimates. The unweighted identity yields the threshold $\mu\leq\frac14$, while employing extra self-similar weight raises the threshold to $\mu<\frac38$ and provides a weighted control, which implies that the solution's BV norm along an outgoing null cone is small, so that Christodoulou's theory of bounded variation solutions gives the extension.

metadata.title: An extension principle for Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system with finite Doppler exponent
metadata.abstract: We prove a new extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar field system. Rather than imposing conditions for mass ratio $2m/r$ as in Christodoulou's small-mass-ratio criterion or as in An--Chen--Singh's proof [1] with $2m/r<3/8$, here we work through a proposal by An-Tan [2] with finite Doppler exponent (blueshift). By conducting two successive blow-up analyses, followed by a stationary comparison and a rigidity argument, we establish the uniform boundness of $\alpha'$ with $\alpha'=\partial_v\alpha/\partial_vr$ and $\alpha=\partial_v(r\phi)/\partial_vr$. This provides the desired extension principle in An-Tan [2] and completes the picture of weak cosmic censorship developed therein. As we were about to release our preprint, Cicortas communicated to us that together with his collaborators, they concomitantly used a different approach to obtain the corresponding extension principle with finite blueshift (Doppler exponent) for the uncharged Einstein-scalar field system. Hence, we decided to put the current paper as an appendix to An-Tan [2], thereby completing the proof of the weak cosmic censorship for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system. At the same time, we are working with Cicortas and his collaborators to write a new preprint containing both approaches for the Einstein-scalar field system.

metadata.title: Crystallographic quotients of Artin braid groups and torus bundles over flat $3$-manifolds
metadata.abstract: For $n\geq3$, let $\overline B_n=B_n/[P_n,P_n]$ be the crystallographic quotient of the Artin braid group, with translation subgroup $\overline P_n=P_n/[P_n,P_n]\cong\mathbb Z^N$, where $N=\binom n2$. We prove that every compact connected flat $3$-manifold $M$, considered up to affine equivalence, is the base of a geometric torus bundle whose total space is a compact flat manifold with fundamental group a Bieberbach subgroup of some $\overline B_n$. More precisely, for every $n\geq n_M$, where $n_M\in\{3,4,5\}$ is an explicit optimal threshold depending on $M$, we construct a Bieberbach subgroup $\Gamma_n(M)\leq\overline B_n$ of dimension $N$ and a complete normal subgroup $K_n(M)\cong\mathbb Z^{N-3}$ consisting of translations such that $$ \Gamma_n(M)/K_n(M)\cong\pi_1(M). $$ We also determine which of the associated torus-bundle group extensions split: for the realizations constructed here, splitting occurs for exactly four of the ten affine-equivalence classes of compact flat $3$-manifolds.

metadata.title: $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth approximation of mod $k$ integral cycles
metadata.abstract: We prove that every mod $k$ integral cycle $T$ of sufficiently high codimension in an oriented Riemannian manifold $\mathcal{M}$ can be approximated in flat norm by a cycle which is a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifold $\Sigma$ of nearly the same area, up to a singular set of codimension 5. If in addition $T$ belongs to a mod $k$ homology class admitting an embedded $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth manifold representative, then $\Sigma$ can be taken fully regular, up to the codimension one stratum of classical singularities. This extends the smooth approximation theory to cycles with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ in stable regimes. Moreover, we provide examples showing the impossibility of locally approximating minimizing cycles by smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifolds, even in homology classes with smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth representatives.

metadata.title: On Meeks' conjecture on disjoint minimal graphs
metadata.abstract: We study disjoint solution pairs $(u,D)$ to the minimal surface equation in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $u=0$ on $\partial D.$ A conjecture of W. Meeks states that at most two such pairs can exist in $\mathbb{R}^n.$ We confirm the conjecture in two complementary cases. For $n\in\{2,3,4,5,6\},$ we prove it under a superlinearity assumption. In dimension $n=2,$ we establish the result under a suitable sublinearity assumption. We also derive estimates on the asymptotic angle of domains supporting nontrivial solutions for $n\geq 3.$

metadata.title: Proof of the Penrose Conjecture for Maximally Parameterized Initial Data Sets
metadata.abstract: We prove the spacetime Penrose inequality for asymptotically flat initial data sets $(M^n,g,k)$ in all dimensions $n\geq 3$, under the dominant energy condition, for data admitting the 'maximally parameterized form' defined in equation (4.7). In this case, the second fundamental form $k$ is locally parameterized by $n(n+1)/2$ functions, giving the same formal local functional degrees of freedom as an arbitrary symmetric $2$-tensor. The proof is based on a new 1-parameter family of generalized Schoen-Yau identities and their gauge-invariant specialization, inspired by the generalized Jang framework of Bray-Khuri [8, 9]. For maximally parameterized data, these identities produce a Riemannian comparison metric \[ \bar g=g+\beta\otimes\beta \] with nonnegative scalar curvature $R_{\bar{g}} \geq 0$. Under a natural nondegeneracy condition (5.7) at the apparent horizon, the comparison metric admits a smooth minimal completion up to $\partial M^n$. Together with suitable asymptotic control, this reduces the Penrose inequality to its Riemannian counterpart. The all-dimensional conclusion uses the Riemannian Penrose theorem of Bi-Zhu [6], together with a minimizing enclosure argument that allows singular boundaries. More generally, in the spirit of [8, 9], we note that the Penrose conjecture follows whenever a certain system of PDEs (3.18) involving $k$ can be solved, in which case our new identity (3.15) immediately implies $R_{\bar{g}} \geq 0$. A natural problem is thus to regularize our degenerate system to prove a general existence theory, thereby proving the Penrose conjecture. Essentially, we believe this is what the OpenAI paper [27] posted last week on October 6, 2026 claims to have done.

metadata.title: Complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors in low dimensions
metadata.abstract: We classify all complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors with complex Killing function $i\mu-\alpha$ on complete Riemannian surfaces, presenting an explicit list of all possible cases. We show that, contrary to previous statements in the literature, there exist complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors on Riemannian surfaces for which $\alpha\mu\not\equiv0$. We illustrate the classification by providing several explicit local, compact, and complete examples, including a complete example for which $\alpha\mu>0$ everywhere. We then move to three dimensions, proving that a spin-c Riemannian three-manifold admits a complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor with complex Killing function $i\mu-\alpha$ if and only if it is a $\mu$-exact trans-Sasakian manifold of type $(\alpha,\mu)$. In addition, we construct a geodesically incomplete Riemannian three-manifold equipped with a complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor for which neither $\mu$ nor $\alpha$ vanishes identically, and then prove that this is not possible if the characteristic vector field of the associated trans-Sasakian structure is complete. These results settle a conjecture by Große and Nakad (Results in Mathematics, 2015) stating that on two- and three-dimensional Riemannian manifolds the complex Killing function of any complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor must be either globally real or globally imaginary.
